Chapter 5 168
Conditional Access optimization agent
The Conditional idx_01faf2f1 Access optimization agent ensures that all users are protected by Conditional
Access policies. It can recommend new policies and update existing policies based on zero trust
best practices. It also creates policy review reports that provide insights that might indicate
policy misconfiguration.
The Conditional Access agent scans the tenant to identify users, applications and agent
identities created in the last 24 hours that are not protected by Conditional Access policies. If it
finds unprotected users, applications or agent identities, it provides recommendations like
creating a new policy or adding users and applications to an existing policy.
The following steps are executed each time the agent runs. These steps do not consume SCUs:
All Conditional Access policies in the tenant are scanned.
Policy gaps and any overlapping policies are identified.
Previous suggestions are reviewed so that the agent does not repeat suggestions.
If the agent identifies something that was not suggested before, the following steps are taken.
These steps consume SCUs:
Policy gaps or pairs of policies that can be consolidated are identified.
Any custom instructions provided by the admin are reviewed.
New policies are created in report-only mode or suggestions are provided to modify
existing policies.
The agent can include the following policy suggestions:
Require MFA: The agent idx_b9ca83a6 identifies users created in the last 24 hours who are not
covered by a Conditional Access policy that enforces MFA. It can also update the policy.
Require device-based controls: The agent can enforce controls such as device
compliance, app protection policies, and domain-joined devices.
Block legacy authentication: The agent blocks user accounts that use legacy
authentication from signing in.
Block device code flow: The agent looks for any policy that blocks device code flow
authentication.
Risky users: The agent checks for a Conditional Access policy that forces password
change for high-risk users. This requires an Entra ID P2 license.
Risky sign-ins: The agent checks for a Conditional Access policy that enforces MFA for
high-risk sign-ins. This requires an Entra ID P2 license.

Adjusting settings
Once the agent has idx_b19d71d3 been enabled, you can adjust its settings by clicking on Settings. The
following settings are available.
Trigger
The agent is scheduled to run every 24 hours from the time it was first enabled. For example, if
you first enable the agent at 1:00 PM, it will run every day at 1:00 PM. This can be changed by
unchecking the box Schedule the agent to run every 24 hours. Once this is done, the agent
can be run manually.

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 5 172
chunks.content:
Chapter 5 172
In addition to running on schedule, the agent can also be enabled to run if there are changes to
turned-on policies by checking the box Automatically analyze tenant each time there are
changes to policies that are turned on.
Microsoft Entra objects to monitor
By default, the agent monitors newly created users and applications. This can be changed by
unchecking the relevant options under this section.
Agent capabilities
This setting specifies whether the agent will create new Conditional Access policies in report-
only mode or not. This setting is on by default. You can turn this off by unchecking the box
Allow agent to autonomously create new policies in report-only mode.
Phased rollout
When the agent creates new policies in report-only mode, the policy is rolled out in phases.
Gradual deployment minimizes the chance of a mass disruption to end users and saves time by
reducing the need for manual analysis and planning. The agent intelligently assigns groups to
different phases; however, administrators can review and edit the group selection.
Administrators can also configure the days between phases. Phased rollout is on by default. It
can be turned off, if required.
Once the agent selects the groups for each phase, it creates a duplicate Conditional Access
policy that only includes the group of the first phase. The original policy remains in report-only
mode to enable administrators to collect data. When the deployment advances to the next
phase, the next batch of groups is added to the enabled Conditional Access policy. The agent
continues to monitor each stage for sign-in failures. If the successful sign-ins drop below 90%,
the agent stops the deployment, and the enabled policy is changed to report-only mode.
Administrators can then review logs to determine the cause of sign-in failures before restarting
the rollout.
Passkey adoption campaigns
The agent can help idx_17768c44 organizations develop adoption campaigns that guide users to adopt
stronger authentication methods. The agent can assess user and device readiness, generate a
deployment plan and guide users through the required steps. It can also create a Conditional
Access policy.
Passkeys must be enabled in the Authentication methods policy in your tenant. Once done
check the box Allow agent to create passkey adoption campaigns. After this setting is
enabled, the agent analyzes the tenant to identify eligible users. Users having privileged
administrator roles are automatically targeted. Once the campaign is ready, it shows up as one
of the suggestions on the agent overview page. From this suggestion, the administrator can
173 AI in Microsoft Entra
adjust the settings like editing the included users list, grace period, and more. They can then
deploy and monitor the campaign.
Once the campaign is active, the agent guides users to adopt passkeys. Users needing device

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 5 172
chunks.content:
updates receive notifications in Microsoft Teams prompting them to update their device, and
users needing to set up a passkey receive notifications in Microsoft Teams with complete
guidance on setting up passkeys. Once at least one user is ready, the agent creates a
Conditional Access policy that enforces passkeys. This policy is created in report-only mode.
Notifications
The agent can send Teams messages to specified users and groups when new suggestions are
available.
Knowledge sources
Organizations can now upload a PDF or Word document containing specific information about
their organization. This can include policies and guidelines. The agent uses these files to
generate suggestions that are more relevant to the organization.
Administrators can also give the agent standing instructions that the agent will consider while
providing suggestions. You could include custom instructions to exclude members of certain
groups from being evaluated for inclusion in a Conditional Access policy. For example, you
might want to exclude guest users from being included in a Conditional Access policy.
Plugins
The agent integrates with ServiceNow and can automatically create a change management
request for each suggestion. The ServiceNow connector needs to be configured for Security
Copilot before the agent can start creating tickets.
Permissions
The agent operates under its own identity. This page shows the permissions the agent identity
has in the tenant.
Review suggestions
The Conditional Access optimization agent provides suggestions to create or update
Conditional Access policies. It also creates reports for activities related to those policies. An
administrator needs to review these suggestions and decide whether to accept or reject them.
Depending on the settings and your environment, the agent might run and not find any
unprotected users or idx_eb3ecf5a applications and hence not recommend any changes. In other cases, it
might find unprotected users or applications and create new Conditional Access policies in
report-only mode, suggest modifying an existing policy, or suggest merging overlapping
policies. With each suggestion, the agent provides detailed reasons for making those
suggestions so admins can make informed decisions. To review any suggestion, click on the

Chapter 5 174
Review suggestion button as shown in Figure 5.9. The following actions can be taken from the
fly out pane as shown in Figure 5.10:
Review the details of the suggestion by clicking on Review policy changes. This page

applied. Policy details can be viewed both in a list format as well as in JSON format,

Microsoft Entra Agent ID
As organizations idx_bd8fa112 accelerate the adoption of AI agents across productivity, security, and
business operations, a critical challenge emerges: how do you manage, secure, and govern
autonomous software that acts on behalf of users and systems? Microsoft Entra Agent ID
addresses this gap by introducing a dedicated identity framework for AI agents, built on top of
the proven Microsoft Entra ID platform.
Unlike traditional application identities or service principals, Agent ID treats AI agents as first-
class identities alongside users, devices, and applications. This means every agent, whether
built in Microsoft Copilot Studio, Azure AI Foundry, or through third-party platforms using the
Entra SDK, receives a verifiable, auditable, and governable digital identity.
The agent identity architecture follows a hierarchical model designed for scalable, centralized
management. Understanding these constructs is essential for IT administrators planning to
onboard AI agents into their identity infrastructure.
Concept Description
Agent Identity
The primary account used by an AI agent to authenticate to
systems and access resources. Agent identities do not have
credentials of their own; they authenticate using tokens issued
by their agent identity blueprint.
Agent Identity Blueprint
A reusable template and authentication foundation in Entra ID.
The blueprint holds credentials, acquires tokens on behalf of all
agent identities created from it, and serves as the policy
enforcement point for Conditional Access.
Blueprint Principal
A service principal object created when a blueprint is registered
in a tenant. It enables the blueprint to acquire tokens and appear
in audit logs within that tenant.
177 AI in Microsoft Entra
Concept Description
Agent User Account
An optional user-type account paired 1:1 with an agent identity.
Required only when the agent must access systems that need a
user object, such as Exchange Online mailboxes or Teams
channels.
Agent Registry
A centralized directory that stores agent metadata, facilitates
controlled discovery, and enables agent-to-agent collaboration
using the A2A protocol. It serves as the authoritative control
plane for all operational agents.
Table 5.1: Agent ID core concepts
Agents created in Microsoft first-party platforms such as Copilot Studio and Azure AI Foundry
automatically receive an Agent ID upon creation and appear in the Entra admin center. For

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 5 176
chunks.content:
non-Microsoft platforms, the Entra SDK for Agent ID enables programmatic registration and
management.
Organizations have historically relied on two identity paradigms: human identities tied to
credentials and lifecycle events, and application identities (service principals) designed for
long-lived, stable services. AI agents break both models:
Dynamic creation at scale: Agents may be spun up and destroyed thousands of times
per day, making manual service principal management impractical.
Autonomous behavior: Agents act without per-request human prompts, requiring
authorization and approval gating that traditional apps do not need.
Hybrid access patterns: Some agents use delegated (on-behalf-of) access, while
others operate autonomously with app-only permissions, and many shift between
both modes.
Agent ID addresses these challenges by providing purpose-built identity constructs that carry
richer context, including metadata such as purpose, environment, and ownership, along with
custom security idx_daa32e6f attributes that integrate directly with policy enforcement.
Microsoft Entra Agent ID extends the full breadth of Entra security controls to agent identities.
The following capabilities are available.

Microsoft Entra idx_268180ee Agent ID extends the same identity, access, and governance controls you
already rely on for your workforce to AI agents. By treating agents as first-class identities,
organizations gain the visibility and policy enforcement needed to scale AI adoption securely.

6
Microsoft Entra Entitlement
Management
Identity Governance (IG) is a critical aspect of modern enterprise security and operational
efficiency. As organizations idx_d897d777 increasingly rely on digital platforms and cloud services, the need
to manage user identities, access rights, and entitlements has become more complex and
essential. Effective identity governance ensures that only authorized individuals have access to
sensitive data and resources, reducing the risk of data breaches, insider threats, and
compliance violations. By implementing robust policies and controls, organizations can
enforce the principle of least privilege, ensuring that users have the minimum level of access
necessary to perform their jobs.
Additionally, identity governance streamlines the onboarding and offboarding processes,
making it easier to grant or revoke access as employees join, move within, or leave the
organization. This not only enhances security but also improves operational agility and user
productivity. Automated identity governance solutions provide continuous monitoring and
auditing capabilities, enabling organizations to detect anomalies and respond to potential
security incidents swiftly.
In this chapter, we will cover:
Microsoft Entra ID Governance
Principle of least privilege
Entitlement management
Access reviews
•
•

Microsoft Entra ID Governance
Microsoft Entra ID Governance is a comprehensive identity governance solution designed to
help organizations idx_7a629bc2 manage, monitor, and control user identities and access within their digital
environments. As the complexity of enterprise infrastructures grows, so does the challenge of
ensuring that only the right individuals have the appropriate levels of access to critical
resources. Microsoft Entra ID Governance addresses these challenges by providing advanced
tools for automating and enforcing access policies, streamlining the user lifecycle, and
maintaining regulatory compliance.
At its core, Microsoft Entra ID Governance empowers organizations to apply the principle of
least privilege, ensuring users are granted only the permissions necessary for their roles. The
platform offers capabilities such as automated provisioning and deprovisioning, access
reviews, entitlement management, and privileged identity management. These features enable
IT administrators to efficiently grant, review, and revoke access as users join, transition, or
leave the organization, reducing the risk of unauthorized access and data breaches.
It helps organizations address the following critical concerns:
Ensuring that users have access to the right resources.
Monitoring how the users are using that access.
Implementing organizational controls to manage access.

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 8, Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management
chunks.content:
Ensuring auditors can verify that the controls are working effectively.
With Microsoft Entra ID Governance, organizations can govern the identity and access lifecycle
while providing secure privileged access for administration.
Each identity follows a lifecycle that begins when a user joins an organization and ends when
they depart. Upon joining, an identity is created—this stage is referred to as the joiner. Users
are then granted access necessary to fulfill their job responsibilities. During their time with the
organization, users may transition between different roles; this is known as the mover stage. At
this point, access must be updated to reflect the requirements of the new role, while access
from previous roles should be revoked. When users leave the organization, their identity is
removed from the system—referred to as the leaver stage—and all associated access to
organizational resources is withdrawn. This process is illustrated in the following figure:

chunks.content:
Chapter 6 186
Figure 6.1: Identity and access lifecycle
Most organizations struggle with managing these changes at scale. They must ensure that the
users' identities idx_15186ea0 are provisioned and reprovisioned quickly and accurately to minimize risk and
to ensure that the users are productive as soon as possible. Using Entitlement Management
Access Packages and Access Reviews features of Microsoft Entra ID Governance,
organizations can manage provisioning of new users at scale, ensuring that users have access
to the resources they need to do their job, maintain user access as they move across roles and
remove access once they leave the organization.
Microsoft Entra idx_7a8ff411 ID Governance allows organizations to meet the following use cases:
Govern employee and guest lifecycle: Governing the lifecycle of employee identities
is the core requirement of effective identity governance. Similar governance processes
also need to be applied to guest accounts in the organization. These guest accounts
could belong to business partners, contractors, or suppliers. Microsoft Entra ID
Governance offers the same capabilities to govern guest user access as it does for
employees.
Govern access to applications: Using the features of Microsoft Entra ID Governance,
organizations can manage access beyond what was originally provisioned for the user.
This also enables the organization to efficiently scale and enforce access policies and
controls on an ongoing basis.
These cases demonstrate the importance of identity governance in maintaining security and
compliance.

The Microsoft Entra ID Governance dashboard displays usage information about the ID
governance features configured in the tenant. It provides an overview of the state of ID
governance including action buttons and links to documentation. It is accessible from the
Entra admin idx_ed17c41f portal by navigating to ID Governance | Dashboard. The following screenshot
shows the dashboard:

that feature.
Whether you are just getting started with ID Governance or have already deployed some
capabilities, this dashboard helps you understand the coverage, identify implementation gaps,
and assists you in assessing the complexity of your IT landscape.
Principle of least privilege
The principle idx_94a57bb4 of least privilege is a foundational concept of identity governance that ensures
users are granted only the minimum access necessary to perform their job functions. By

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 6 186
chunks.content:
limiting permissions, organizations can reduce the risk of accidental or malicious misuse of
sensitive data and resources. This approach helps contain potential security breaches, as
compromised accounts are restricted in what they can access. Implementing least privilege
also supports compliance with regulatory requirements by enforcing strict access controls.

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 6 188
chunks.content:
Chapter 6 188
Regularly reviewing and adjusting user permissions is essential to maintain this principle,
especially as employees change roles or leave the organization, ensuring that unnecessary
access is promptly revoked.
The following idx_3d5cc6b8 are some key concepts of the principles of least privilege:
Access to only the required resources: This is the foundation of the principle of least
privilege. Users are given access to resources only if they have a genuine need to access
those resources to fulfill their job duties. This prevents unauthorized data access and
limits the impact of a security breach. Lifecycle workflows is a feature in identity
governance that helps organizations automate lifecycle processes.
Role-based Access Control (RBAC): Access is based on the role and job functions of
the user. Each role has the minimum permissions assigned that are necessary to fulfill
job requirements. Microsoft Entra RBAC manages access to Microsoft Entra resources.
Just-In-Time access: Users are granted access to resources only for the duration for
which they are needed and revoked when they are no longer required. This minimizes
idx_11d7bb38 the timeframe during which attackers could potentially exploit elevated privileges.
Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management is a solution that helps manage,
control, and monitor just-in-time access.
Regular audit and review: Organizations must perform periodic reviews of user
access to ensure that they still require the permissions that they have. This helps
ensure that there is no permission creep. Access reviews is a feature in Microsoft Entra
ID Governance that helps organizations automate access reviews.
Default deny: The principle of least privilege works on default deny. This means that,
by default, users are denied access, and access is explicitly granted only for approved
purposes.
By following these principles, organizations can reduce risk and ensure alignment with
business needs.
Entitlement management
When users join an organization, they require access to various resources such as SharePoint
sites, Teams channels, and applications. New employees may not initially know which
resources are idx_8d0eadf3 necessary. After joining, they often need time to determine what access is
required and to identify the appropriate approvers for their access requests. This process can
delay the point at which the employee becomes fully productive. The situation can become
more complex when collaborating with other organizations, as it may be unclear who in the
external organization requires access to specific resources.
•
•
•
•
•
189 Microsoft Entra Entitlement Management
Entitlement management is a Microsoft Entra ID Governance feature designed to streamline
identity and access lifecycle management for both users and guests. It automates the processes

of requesting and assigning access by utilizing access packages, which are organized within
catalogs to oversee and maintain user access.
Understanding catalogs
A catalog is a idx_1c66de43 container of resources and access packages. A catalog is created when all related
resources need idx_36a8687c to be grouped together. For example, you might want to group all marketing
resources into one catalog. This catalog might include Microsoft 365 (M365) groups and teams
related to marketing, marketing SharePoint sites, and some marketing applications. This
catalog can then be used to create access packages for marketing users. An access package
might contain all or a subset of resources from the catalog.
By default, a Global Administrator and Identity Governance Administrator can manage all
aspects of entitlement management such as creating catalogs and access packages. However,
they may not know to which business resources access has to be granted and for how long.
This is further complicated as each business unit may have different requirements. An IT
administrator can delegate the task of creating and assigning catalogs and access packages to
administrators in the business units.
There are three ways of delegating access.
The Identity Governance Administrator can create the catalog and then assign catalog
owners to add resources and manage the catalog going forward.
If resources don't have owners, administrators can create catalogs and add the
resources. They can then assign catalog owners to manage the catalog going forward.
If resources have owners, administrators can grant the Catalog Creator role to non-IT
administrators who can then create their own catalogs.
Understanding access packages
An access idx_b6a80592 package is a bundle of all resources that employees might need to idx_0f206748 perform their job
duties. The following resources can be included in an access package:
Microsoft Entra security groups
M365 Groups and Teams
Microsoft Entra enterprise applications
SharePoint Online sites
Microsoft Entra roles (Preview)
Azure Resources (Preview)
API Permissions

defined based on which the assignment of the access package can be controlled.

Connected organizations
A connected organization is an external organization that your organization works with and
needs to idx_e97ff4af share resources such as applications idx_1f2df4df and SharePoint sites. Mostly, users in external
organizations do not exist in your Microsoft Entra directory. You can use entitlement
management to bring them into your directory as needed.
Connected organizations provide a way for users in these external organizations to request an
access package and be able to access applications and SharePoint sites. There are four methods
for defining users that make up a connected organization:
Users from another Microsoft Entra tenant.
Users from a non-Microsoft directory configured for SAML/WS-Fed IdP federation.
Users from a non-Microsoft directory whose email addresses share the same domain
name. Email one-time passcode authentication must be enabled for these users to
idx_248fcbe5 allow authentication when requesting access idx_0d0ba7cc and later when accessing resources.
Users with a Microsoft account such as hotmail.com.
Using connected organizations, administrators do not need to invite individual guest users to
their tenant.

Auto-assigning users to an access package
In some situations, you might want to automatically add users to access packages based on
their idx_99069cca Microsoft Entra ID attributes. For example, you might want to add all users in the
marketing department to the Marketing access package. Follow the steps below to auto-assign
an access package based on user attributes:
Log in to https://entra.microsoft.com and navigate to ID Governance |
Entitlement management.
Click on Access packages and select the access package to which you want to assign
users.
Click on Policies.
Click on Add auto assignment policy.
Click on Edit next to the Rule Syntax. Select the user property from the Property drop
down and select the appropriate Operator. In the Value box, type in the value of the
user property. See example in Figure 6.25. Click Save to save the rule.
The boxes to Automatically create assignments and Automatically remove
assignments are already checked. Doing this ensures that the users are automatically
added and removed from the access package as their configured Microsoft Entra ID
attributes change. For example, when a new user joins the Marketing department, they
will be automatically added to this access package based on their Entra ID user
attribute. Now, if the user moves from Marketing to Sales and their Entra ID user
attribute is updated, they will be automatically removed from this access package and
lose access to all resources that this access package idx_fff39d51 grants access to. You can also
configure a grace period to retain user access to this access package for a pre-defined
period once they go out of scope. Refer to the following screenshot. Click on Next.

Understanding access reviews
Using Microsoft Entra ID, users in the organization can collaborate with other internal users
and with idx_c780c8a0 external guests. The self-service capabilities in Microsoft Entra ID make it easy for
internal users and external guests to request and receive access to resources. However, this
poses a new challenge: users may have access to resources for longer than required or have
more access than required to do their job. Checks and balances should be in place to ensure
that users need continued access to the resources. Using access reviews, organizations can
review users' access to security and M365 groups, applications, access packages, Microsoft
Entra roles, and Azure resource roles. Some scenarios where access reviews could be used are:
There are idx_f734a59a too many users in privileged roles.
Automation is not possible. For example, HR data cannot be synchronized with
Microsoft Entra ID.

If you want to repurpose a group for a different use.
When users have access to business-critical data or applications, you might want to
periodically review their access to ensure their job role still requires them to access that
data or application.
The following idx_e094816f are some key features of access reviews:
They can be ad-hoc or scheduled.
They can be delegated to non-IT administrators or business owners.
Users can self-attest their access or reviewers can be designated.
Insights can be used to decide whether a user's access should be continued or
discontinued.
Outcomes such as continuing or removing access can be automated.
They can be tracked for compliance or policy reasons.
The following idx_bfa05023 figure shows the access review workflow:
Figure 6.26: Access review workflow
The administrator creates access reviews in the Entra portal. Once the access review starts, the
users and resource owners receive requests to review the access. They review current
memberships and make decisions about keeping or revoking access.
